_meta.title: Per-frame compute inventory of the pose / person-crop modules on their monthly test-set checkouts
_meta.method: Read-only audit of the checkout that scripts.testset.profiles.profile(<module>) resolves (module_dir, else external/<module>). Weight files hashed with sha256 (first 16 hex kept). Architectures taken from the code and, for weight files, from a non-executing scan of the pickle class references and tensor shapes (no unpickling of objects, no torch import) and from the ONNX graph header. mmpose behaviour read from the overlay that the test set runs (out/envs/mmpose1, mmpose 1.3.1). No module, model or GPU code was run.
_meta.line_references: file:line relative to the module checkout unless a path is given; mmpose paths are relative to out/envs/mmpose1/mmpose/.
_meta.frame_size: one decoded 1920x1080x3 uint8 frame = 6 220 800 B (about 6.2 MB); buffer sizes below are frame counts from the code times this size

risk_classes.NEAR: small numeric change (export, fp16, changed batch composition without deterministic kernels)

_meta.brief_costs: median ms per recorded frame from the batch test-set runs on a contended machine, as given in the task brief (not measured here); early-exiting modules look cheaper per recorded frame than per active frame
sources_used: docs/analysis/module_consumption.md/.json (default branches; re-verified here on the actual checkouts)
docs/arch_review/REVIEW_DETAILED.md (M11, M13, M15, M16, M23, M26, M27)

facts: All eight checkouts carry the same cv_common/utils/datasets.py (sha256 94e2577e800c283f, substituted cv_common ac5098d2) and db_worker/ML_worker.py (5a2aadf511e20699).

VideoWorker.load_source opens LoadImages(source, img_size=1280) (db_worker/ML_worker.py:225-238; cv_common/global_config.yaml:4); LoadImages reads CAP_PROP_FRAME_COUNT at open (cv_common/utils/datasets.py:282-285).

get_im0s(n) = get_frame(n)[2] (datasets.py:279-280). get_frame decodes forward only: cap.grab() for every skipped frame, cap.read() for the requested one, asserts n >= last loaded frame, caches the last frame (datasets.py:235-277).

get_frame and __next__ also build a YOLOv5 letterbox to 1280 plus a CHW/RGB contiguous copy on every decoded frame (datasets.py:226-231, 267-272); none of the eight modules uses it (they take im0s only).
get_frame / __next__ print one line per decoded frame (datasets.py:217, 265).
cap.read() returns a new array per decode (datasets.py:205, 258), so a frame held by reference is not overwritten by later decodes.

load_metadata opens both ndjson files and yields one parsed GM line and one parsed tracker line per frame (db_worker/ML_worker.py:240-280); a second load_metadata() call re-opens and re-parses from frame 1.

Track().from_json is a dict update (cv_common/track.py:19-21); restoring an airplane or vehicle calls TrackedObject.from_state_dict, which copies the dict and converts _p0 (up to 250 points) and _st to numpy on every call (cv_common/tracked_object.py:604-636; transport.py:129-145). Observed on a production tracker file: _p0 list length mean 206, max 250 (docs/analysis/ndjson_observed.json).
The test-set runner always passes a real JsonLogger with filename None (scripts/run_module.py:284), so every module writes <module dir>/None.ndjson; production passes json_fn.

JsonLogger.update appends Python lists per box/text/keypoint set and, whenever the frame id changes, serialises the previous frame as an ndjson row (cv_common/log_utils.py:85-88, 90-123). state_dict=True extracts 4 fields only (log_utils.py:45-60), but callers that pass obj.to_state_dict() first serialise the whole object (tracked_object.py:538-600).
plot_one_box returns immediately when img is None (cv_common/utils/plots.py:30-33).
TrackedObject.draw_OF_points loops over up to 250 optical-flow points calling cv2.circle even when img is None (cv_common/tracked_object.py:511-516).

inference_topdown runs init_default_scope and builds Compose(test pipeline) from the config on every call (apis/inference.py:155-158), runs the pipeline per bbox, then one model.test_step for all bboxes of the call: one batch per call (apis/inference.py:179-196).

Per bbox: GetBBoxCenterScale padding 1.25 (datasets/transforms/common_transforms.py:52), TopdownAffine fixes the aspect ratio to the input size and cv2.warpAffine INTER_LINEAR from the full image passed in (datasets/transforms/topdown_transforms.py:56-118), PackPoseInputs; normalisation and BGR->RGB on the device in PoseDataPreprocessor.

flip_test=True in both pose configs used here: TopdownPoseEstimator.predict runs extract_feat twice per call (inputs and inputs.flip(-1)) (models/pose_estimators/topdown.py:102-104); heads average both (models/heads/heatmap_heads/heatmap_head.py:253-263; models/heads/coord_cls_heads/simcc_head.py:259-273).

module_preprocessing.same: full-frame CLAHE (BGR->LAB, CLAHE clip 4.0 tiles 16x16 on L, LAB->BGR) with identical code and bbox = person track box add_offset(0.1, 0.1), batch = all selected persons of the frame: hand-signals main.py:43-51 and :537; lead-marshaller path A main.py:295-303 and :161; wing-walkers helpers.py:208-216 and main.py:243
module_preprocessing.different: steering: YCrCb equalizeHist of the add_offset(0.2, 0.1) region pasted into a copy of the frame, one bbox per call (main.py:510-527); lead-marshaller path B: raw buffered frame, raw track box, no CLAHE (main.py:594-613)

identical_models.stage_windows: lead-marshaller A: airplane visible before arrival; hand-signals: after arrival until departure (BL approaches); steering: up to 240 s after arrival; wing-walkers: departure movement. Only hand-signals and steering overlap in time, and their preprocessing differs, so sharing is one model instance, not shared results.

present_not_loaded_in_several_checkouts.note: named only in cv_common/global_config.yaml:96-97 (mmpose 0.x config); none of the eight active code paths loads it

same_architecture_different_weights_or_p: torchvision swin_t x2 in safety-vests (3-class orientation with mean/std normalisation; 2-class vest without normalisation; different crops)
torchvision resnet18 x2 in safety-vests (2-class presence gate at 192x192 bicubic; 1-logit v4 small-band CNN at 224x112)
torchvision efficientnet_b0 x2 referenced by hair-policy (both 2-class heads; preprocessing not readable)

COCO-17 keypoint models on person crops: HRNet-W48 (four modules), SimCC-ResNet50 288x384 (pin-verification), MoveNet SinglePose Thunder 256x256 (fod-walk, uses shoulder x order only), YOLOv8m-pose (safety-vests v4 gate, uses shoulders only)
shared_frame_hazards: fod-walk@dev draws in place on the cached decoded frame when write_video is False (main.py:145-146, 162-176, 225-227). Before decoded frames are shared between modules in one real-time process this must be removed (fod-walk candidate F-E2).
Holding frames by reference instead of copying (steering S-E1, lead-marshaller L-E1) is exact only while no module writes into shared frames.

invocation.condition: after airplane.arrived and before departured (main.py:861-870), no active stopped beltloader found (:886), beltloader_track_delay > 60 frames (:888-889), workers ROI defined, at least one person whose bottom-centre is in the ROI (:530-538). (a) Immediate: if a beltloader track taller than 50 px is not STOPPED (:523-524) -> pose on this frame (:553-567). (b) Replay: when a new active stopped beltloader id appears with roi_present and it was in the moving history (:646-650) -> check_hand_signals runs pose on every buffered frame older than frame-40 whose persons are not yet in the history (:338-364).
invocation.calls_per_frame_in_window: (a) 1 call per frame; (b) on the replay frame, one call per buffered frame in (frame-240, frame-40], up to about 200 calls
invocation.batched: per frame yes; the replay frames are processed as separate sequential calls
